pr_title: ESQL: Account for an exception being thrown when building a BytesRefArrayBlock
pr_body:
Account for an exception being thrown when building a BytesRefArrayBlock by registering an empty BytesRef in the BytesRefArray, rather than doing nothing and confusing the BytesRefArray content.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99472.
pr_comments: Hi @astefan, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> This is, also, fixing #99475.

Actually that bug doesn't reproduce anymore. Without this fix and, also, without https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99685.

issue_context.title: ESQL: issue using coalesce and to_ip functions
comments:
There are  multiple issues here:
- `Unknown column [x2], did you mean [x1]` is more generic and has nothing to do with those specific functions. It's about `ResolveRefs` analyzer rule that "stops" resolving references further. Instead it's covering a set of special cases where the same column gets renamed multiple times (`from test | rename age as abc, age as xyz`)
- `text` type fields (like `ip1` here) return an empty array of multi-values `[]` when there is no value in that document for that specific field, instead they should return `null`.
- the `to_ip` function receives the empty value from the `text` field above and fails to convert it.

`Failed trying to format bytes as IP address.  Possibly caused by a mapping mismatch` is coming from the attempt to convert `127.00.1` to an IP. The warning is included in the response headers but the exception still goes through, instead of just converting the value to `null`, not failing and still seeing the warning in the response header.

For data like

```
{ "index": { } }
{ "emp_no": 20, "ip1": "127.0", "ip2": "0.1" }
{ "index": { } }
{ "emp_no": 50 }
```

and query `FROM test | eval x1 = concat(ip1, ip2), x2 = coalesce(x1, \"255.255.255.255\"), x3 = to_ip(x2) | keep x3, x3, x1, x2` and using `?format=json` the node dies with assertion error

review_comments: Because the warnings were just copied when the `null` parameter testcase was generated, instead of just checking the `null` value is returned, the warnings were also checked and the tests failed where in fact there were no warnings expected.

These warnings ended up failing the null parameter tests I mentioned [above](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/99726/files#r1332253400), when in fact they were only needed when the parameter **was not null**.
